title: Tracelet cost & latency sketchbook
content:
Objective:
Capture a set of rough UX ideas and lightweight wireframes for a token-level cost + latency investigation surface that ties into invocation traces ("tracelets") and makes it fast for engineers and SREs to find costly or slow invocations and understand root cause without leaving the Console. This doc is intentionally exploratory — sketches, trade-offs, and backlog items.

Goals (why this view):
- Reduce mean time to identify cost/latency hotspots by surfacing per-invocation token breakdowns and traces.
- Make the cost story actionable: show per-token cost attribution, top contributing tokens/phrases, and likely causes (batching, kernel, queue).
- Connect quickly to remediations: model pinning, quantization toggles, cache policy adjustments, rollout fallback.

Primary users:
- Platform engineers diagnosing high-tail latency for customer routes.
- ML engineers investigating quality regressions tied to quantization or model variants.
- Customer success when explaining billing spikes to customers.

Assumptions and instrumentation required:
- Each invocation emits: invocation_id, route, customer_id, model_version, model_variant, region, device_type, start_ts, end_ts, queue_ms, kernel_ms, kv_cache_hit (bool), input_tokens, output_tokens, per_token_cost_usd, batch_id, sequence_length, prompt_slice_tags (optional).
- Traces link invocation_id -> lower-level kernel/executor spans (SRE traces).
- Existing token-level instrumentation exists but may need an attribution sampler to avoid high cardinality for all invocations.

High-level interaction flows (sketches):
1) Investigator starts on a top-level route heatmap or alerts list and clicks an invocation row -> opens Tracelet panel (right-side overlay).
2) Tracelet panel header: brief invocation metadata (time, route, model, cost, latency, status) + quick actions (open full trace, copy invocation id, flag & annotate).
3) Main area: dual view toggles (Cost-first | Latency-first).
   - Cost-first: stacked waterfall by token groups (prompt/system, user prompt slices, response tokens) showing cumulative cost per token segment. Hover shows per-token cost, sample token text, and token index.
   - Latency-first: token-timeline heatmap (x-axis token index, y-axis pipeline stages: queue, kernel, kernel-attention, kv-load). Color intensity = ms.
4) Below charts: breadcrumbed trace links to underlying GPU/kernel spans with expandable rows showing host, device, kernel name, kernel duration, and memory copy times.
5) Rightmost column: quick remediation suggestions (auto-suggested) and related invocations (same batch, same user, same model variant).

Wireframe notes (frame-by-frame):
- Header area (compact): Route name | Model variant chip | Invocation timestamp | cost ($0.00) | total latency (ms) | status badge
- Chart area split horizontally: top = cost waterfall (svg stacked bar with token grouping), bottom = latency timeline (compact heatmap). Toggle label shown prominently.
- Hover card: small popup with token snippet (up to 120 chars), token index, token_type (input/output), cost_usd, latency_ms_breakdown (queue/kernel/kv). Copy button copies token text & index.
- Token selection interaction: click a contiguous token range to create a "slice" — tool highlights that slice across both charts and offers actions: re-run against quantization profile, simulate caching policy, link to eval set.
- Breadcrumb & path: left of overlay show path back to Route / Time range / Alert id.

Novel visual elements to prototype:
- Waterfall mini-brush: allow selecting a cost threshold (e.g., highlight tokens that cumulatively contribute 80% of cost).
- Kernel-sourcing ribbon: a thin ribbon above timeline that signals which kernel (e.g., fused-attn-v2) was in use for each token index (if kernel switching occurred mid-invocation).
- Batch-map toggle: show grouping of invocation into batches with per-batch median latencies; clicking a batch zooms to batch-level trace.

Acceptance criteria for initial prototype (Phase 0):
- Open overlay from invocation row with header and two stub charts populated from sampled invocation payloads.
- Hover card shows token snippet + cost estimate.
- Able to copy invocation id and open full trace in tracing system.
- All UI elements respond correctly at desktop widths; mobile not required.

MVP (Phase 1) scope suggestions:
- Full token-level waterfall and latency timeline for sampled invocations.
- Token-slice creation and copy-of-token-text action.
- Basic remediation suggestions (link to model pin, quantization recommendation screen).
- Filter bar: time range, model, region, status, cost threshold.
- Backend: sampled API endpoint that returns token attribution and linked trace ids.

Phase 2 (polish / scale):
- Aggregation mode: show aggregated token-attribution heatmap for large sets (e.g., 1000 invocations) with percentiles.
- Automated anomaly detection: suggested slices that explain >X% cost delta.
- Customer-facing export: generate a short PDF report with top 3 slices and suggested fixes.

Backlog / work items (rough):
- PROTO-01: Sketch overlay and basic chrome (1 designer day).
- API-TRACELET-1: Sampled tracelet API prototype (backend) (3 eng days).
- UI-TRACELET-2: Cost waterfall component (react + svg) (5 eng days).
- UI-TRACELET-3: Latency timeline heatmap component (4 eng days).
- SRE-OBS-4: Trace linking helper & RBAC checks (2 eng days).
- DATA-PIPE-6: Ensure token attribution fields in event schema & sampling policy (3 eng days).
- EVAL-UX-9: Connect token slices to eval harness for offline repro (3 eng days).
- QA-TRACE-10: Synthetic invocation generator for UI e2e tests (2 qa days).

Priority matrix (quick):
- High: Trace linking, sampled API, basic waterfall hover.
- Medium: Token slice actions, remediation suggestions.
- Low: Aggregation mode, PDF export, mobile layout.

Edge cases & questions to resolve:
- Sampling policy: how do we price the instrumentation overhead for very high QPS routes? (sampling vs on-demand capture).
- PII handling: tokens may contain sensitive data — need redact rules and masked hover cards by default.
- Cardinality: prompt_slice_tags could explode dimensions — design filters to avoid UI overload.
- Cache hit semantics: when kv_cache_hit=true, attribution should show less kernel time but still show latency waiting on cache loads.
- Can token indexes be mapped back to original prompt slices reliably after normalization?

Design trade-offs discussed:
- Full fidelity token text in hover vs redaction for compliance. Proposed default: show masked text with first/last 3 chars, full text available only to users with compliance role.
- Always-on token collection vs on-demand capture. Proposed default: sample 1/1000 invocations for full token capture + allow "capture next N invocations" button for on-demand repro.

Example queries / debug snippets to prototype in backend:
- SQL to find invocations that have > $0.10 per invocation and kernel_ms > 200:
  SELECT invocation_id, route, model_version, per_invocation_cost, kernel_ms
  FROM invocation_metrics
  WHERE per_invocation_cost > 0.10 AND kernel_ms > 200
  ORDER BY per_invocation_cost DESC
  LIMIT 50;

- Aggregate to find top token-level contributors (pseudo):
  SELECT token_text, SUM(per_token_cost_usd) as total_cost, count(*) as occurrences
  FROM token_attributions_sampled
  WHERE event_ts BETWEEN $start AND $end
  GROUP BY token_text
  ORDER BY total_cost DESC
  LIMIT 100;

Design TODOs for next week:
- Run 2 quick hallway tests with SRE/ML eng to validate the waterfall vs timeline framing (Ethan + Maya).
- Wire up the sample API prototype with a stubbed payload (Noah).
- Prepare a short Confluence page summarizing instrumentation needs and compliance checklist (Sofia).
- Bring the mock to next product sync and get buy/no-buy from customer success (Priya to own).

Notes from sketch session (2026-01-15):
- SRE team prefers a compact header and ability to pin a tracelet to the main Console panel for continuous monitoring of a problematic route.
- ML engs want an easy way to mark tokens as "semantic anchors" (used for reranking / instructions) and persist that as a slice for future evals.
- CS asked for a "billing explain" mode that can anonymize, condense and surface the top 3 cost drivers for a customer's bill.

Open decisions for product-review:
- Should remediation suggestions be product-driven (links to settings) or prescriptive (one-click toggles)?
- Sampling defaults: 1/1000 vs 1/10000? We need infra input on storage costs.
- Export: internal-only vs customer-facing? Security/compliance will likely gate customer exports.

References & inspiration:
- Internal: CONFLUENCE-UI-5642 (console trace UX spec), JIRA-UI-1298 (token instrumentation backlog).
- External: "Flamegraph for tokens" design notes from a community post (link archived in Confluence).

Appendix: example stubbed payload for UI dev (one-line JSON string, full schema in Confluence):
  {invocation_id: 'i-20260115-9843', route: 'chat-complete', model_version: 'rw-3b-v2', input_tokens: 37, output_tokens: 173, per_token_cost_usd: 0.000012, kernel_ms: 322, queue_ms: 12, kv_cache_hit: false, tokens_sample: [{index:0, text:'Assistant:', cost_usd:0.000004, kernel_ms:2}, ...]}

If you're reading this and want to prototype a specific visualization, drop a note in the linked Slack thread (see linked_artifacts) or ping @maya in #product-console.

-- end sketchbook --
